newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour says will be firm on public pay.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour says will be firm on public pay.

text.p: The UK opposition Labour Party's finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Friday a future Labour government would take a firm approach to public sector pay, and settlements would have to be made within tough cash limits.
"Labour will take a firm and fair approach to public sector pay," he said in a speech to businessmen in London.
"Decisions will be made with a view to retain, recruit and motivate staff. But these must be made wuithin tough cash limits."
Brown said all public sector pay agreements must be financed from within the agreed departmental cash limits upon which departments must now plan.
He was speaking after recommendations on public sector pay made by the review bodies were leaked to newspapers.
The Financial Times said the bodies have recommended awards ranging from 3.2 to 3.4 percent.
They will formally report to the government next week.
According to the report nurses would receive on average around 3.3 percent, the armed forces about the same, teachers around 3.25 percent and doctors about 3.4 percent.

Brown said public debt had doubled since 1990. "So there can be no blank checks because there is no escape from facing up to the mountain of Tory debt. After our decision on the royal yacht no one can doubt the consistency of this tough approach."
He said Labour would implement a comprehensive spending review if it wins power in the election, due to be held by May.

"The objective will be to investigate how we can reshape expenditure into the next century on the basis of principles most of us would accept -- a commitment not just to encouraging work and a fair society but also to investment in our future."
